newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian shares end up, some second-tier strong.
newsitem.headline: Russian shares end up, some second-tier strong.

text.p: Leading Russian shares ticked down on Thursday afternoon to close slightly up for the day, bolstered by second tier shares which showed some strong gains.
The Russian Trading System 23-share index closed up 0.86 percent at 334.48 after 331.64 on Wednesday on $36.6 million market volume.
GAZ auto maker rose to $36.00 from $26.00 on 6,000 shares traded and Murmanskelectrosvyaz telecom rose to $50.00 from $44.25 on March 7, when it last traded.
Gazprom GAZP.RTS ticked up to $0.650 from $0.642 and LUKoil fell to $14.00 from $14.52.
Traders said that strong moves by leading shares were unlikely on Friday despite the possibility of new cabinet announcements by President Boris Yeltsin and Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin.
"The announcement of reformers is already priced in," said Peter Kizenko, chief equities trader at ING Barings. "There might be a short upward blip, but there is not going to be a sharp rally."
He said the market had felt weaker in the afternoon than in the morning and was likely to open weaker and drift through the day.
Traders said that Western investors were not selling but waiting to invest although strong interest in second-tier oil companies and lower tier telecoms and energos was seen.
